principle_A: Build a definition from the constructor that takes the data already at hand rather than through an intermediate isomorphism, and do not keep both.
A relation that only serves as the `≤` instance is inlined into the instance, not given its own structure.
Statements should elaborate without explicit `@` application.
A constructor with many fields takes a structure of its data, so users get a skeleton from code actions.
rule: convenient constructors for a new type in common use cases

principle_A: A Decidable instance should evaluate efficiently, not re-evaluate the predicate quadratically.
rule: code performance: avoid slow elaboration

principle_A: State results in simp-normal form (`1`, not `exp 0`).
rule: normal forms: settle on a standard form and register simp lemmas towards it

principle_A: Prefer a characterisation of `range (map f g)` over a specialised monotonicity consequence.
rule: strong conclusions

principle_A: Long proofs are split, with the interesting estimates as their own lemmas.
rule: long proofs split into supporting lemmas or definitions

principle_A: State a result as an iff when the converse holds.
rule: strong conclusions (the iff form is not itself stated)

principle_A: Factor a reusable step into a general dot-notation lemma.
rule: split into supporting lemmas

principle_A: Separate a construction from its application: define the general operation on generators and derive the special case.
rule: general definitions

principle_A: Prefer a direct computation over a bounded search when one exists.
Provide the basic API (`const`, `congr`) from which specialised lemmas follow, and reserve the canonical names for the basic ones.
rule: new definitions come with lemmas; API for new definitions

principle_A: Develop general API rather than a specialised lemma.
rule: new definitions come with lemmas; API for new definitions

principle_A: State results as characterisations independent of a particular instance construction.
Do not quantify over a universe of index types inside a class; then extensionality is a theorem, not a field.
Formalise the recurring mathematical concept (adjacent sequences) rather than the ad hoc instance.
rule: general definitions

principle_A: Define the object you will reason about (the iterated sequence) directly, not only one step.
A definition made with `choose` comes with lemmas exposing its `choose_spec` properties.
rule: results using choice become definitions; definitions come with lemmas

principle_A: State the strongest natural consequence (an isomorphism) rather than partial facts.
rule: strong conclusions

principle_A: State lemmas with expanded functions rather than compositions.
Introduce a definition at its most general level, with API, or leave a TODO.
rule: general definitions; API for new definitions

principle_A: Provide the universe-polymorphic `OfSize` form of a preservation instance.
rule: category theory universes

principle_A: Express a property of objects as an `ObjectProperty` and state conditions with `IsIso`, not bespoke structures.
Extract an inline construction into an auxiliary definition.
rule: split into supporting lemmas or definitions

principle_A: Define the general functorial object (iteration as a functor) instead of ad hoc recursive definitions.
rule: general definitions

principle_A: When a structure extends another, define the extended one directly rather than in two stages.
A fact used inside a proof is its own lemma.
rule: split into supporting lemmas

principle_A: Give a default instance by its canonical construction, not through a general helper.
State a result as an iff when the converse holds.
rule: strong conclusions (the iff form is not itself stated)

principle_A: Generalise the core of a proof to a lemma about the underlying general construction.
rule: a different proof structure using existing lemmas; generality
